title: New York's property-tax cap and Riverhead's overrides

capBasics.law: Chapter 97 of the Laws of 2011, codified for towns at General Municipal Law §3-c. The State Comptroller publishes the levy-limit formula and collects the annual local-government tax-cap filing.
capBasics.limit: The tax cap limits the property-tax levy, not a home's tax rate. The allowable levy growth factor — the lesser of inflation or 2%, but never below 1.00 — is only one input. The full local-government calculation also uses the prior levy, tax-base growth, PILOT adjustments, available carryover, transfers of function and statutory exclusions before arriving at the final levy limit.
capBasics.override: A town can lawfully adopt a levy above its calculated levy limit if it first enacts an override local law by at least 60% of the governing body's voting power. Authorizing an override does not itself require the final adopted levy to exceed the limit; it can be adopted as procedural protection while the budget is still being reduced.

finding.headline: Riverhead's independent auditor reported that the Town exceeded its tax levy limit for 2018–2022 without adopting the required override local law.
finding.cause: The auditor traced the issue to a tax-cap calculation error beginning with the 2018 fiscal year that carried forward.
finding.auditQuote: The Town exceeded the 2% property tax cap for the year ended December 31, 2022 without adopting a local law in accordance with the New York State enacted Chapter 97, Laws of 2011 Real Property Tax Levy Cap and Mandate Relief Provisions.
finding.correction: For 2023 and subsequent adopted budgets shown here, the Town used an override local law before adopting a levy above the calculated limit.

implications.title: The 2% figure is not the final Riverhead levy limit
implications.text: For 2027, OSC has set the allowable levy growth factor at 2% for calendar-year local governments. Riverhead's final filed limit still depends on the rest of the statutory formula.

implications.title: An override is authorization, not an outcome
implications.text: A 60% override local law preserves the Board's legal ability to adopt an above-limit levy. Officials can still reduce the budget and ultimately adopt a levy at or below the calculated limit.

implications.title: Historical compliance should come from the filed/audited record
implications.text: A General Fund growth percentage is useful context but cannot by itself prove whether the Town complied with the tax cap, because the statutory test is town-wide and includes formula adjustments and exclusions.

implications.title: 2027 should be updated when Riverhead files its calculation
implications.text: Until the Town's 2027 tax-cap filing is available, a 2% scenario belongs in the site as a planning benchmark — not as a claim that Riverhead's legal ceiling has already been determined.

levyContext.note: General Fund tax levy by year. This is directional growth context only; the statutory tax-cap calculation applies to the covered town-wide levy and incorporates formula adjustments and exclusions.
